newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom aims to mimic D.Telekom hit.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom aims to mimic D.Telekom hit.

text.p: Marcel Michelson
France Telecom chairman Michel Bon said on Monday he hoped his company's pending market flotation would be as popular a success as Deutsche Telekom's share listing today.
"I hope that our market introduction will be as much a popular success as Deutsche Telekom's," he said.
The French state-owned operator will accelerate national and international long distance rate cuts in 1997, after a 25 percent decline in 1996, to make them the cheapest in Europe.

Bon said he expected a fierce public debate in the coming months about the thorny issue of interconnection charges -- the prices France Telecom can charge its future rival telecoms operators in France.

But he noted that when the first tranche of France Telecom shares were put on the market, possibly as soon as in April, the company's interconnection price list would be known which would remove a lot of uncertainty for future investors. The government is expected to sell an initial 20 percent stake.
Bon was speaking at a news conference called to inaugurate a new catagory of telephone numbers called indigo numbers.
France Telecom gives key catagories of numbers colour codes such as green for toll free and various shades of blue for special rate numbers.
The first indigo number will be used by retailer Pinault-Printemps-Redoute as a national number for its all its regional client services.
"When France Telecom was still a branch of the civil service we were immortal, but today our future lies in the hands of our clients," Bon said, hailing the contract with the retailer.
He said he hoped French companies would make more use of the "green" toll-free number, noting there were only 20,000 such numbers in France against over a million in the United States.
Asked whether France Telecom aimed to take a cross-stake in its German partner, Bon said that this could only take place when both companies were listed.
"We said that we would do that after the market had given a valuation of both companies. I note today that the market has given Deutsche Telekom a very high value," Bon said.
He said that Deutsche Telekom's share price also reflected the risk for the German company's future earnings based on the fact that Germany has not yet settled the issue of interconnection charges.

Deutsche Telekom opened bourse trade in Frankfurt on Monday at 33.20 marks, well above its issue price of 28.50 marks, before going on to add a further 70 pfennigs to 33.90 marks at the bourse close after almost 38 million shares changed hands.

In France, Post and Telecommunications minister Francois Fillon has written to the main current and future players in the field soliciting their comments on interconnection before November 30. In a statement, the ministry said it was preparing two decrees to be published at the start of 1997.
"France will be the only European country where the interconnection charges will be known before the national operator is put on the market," Bon said.

Bon said he expected a fierce public battle about the charges. "The period will be interesting, the debate ferocious," Bon said, warning journalists against far-fetched statements that might be made by parties concerned during coming months.

The interconnection prices are very important for the business models of new rivals in telecommunications such as the Cegetel venture of Generale des Eaux, Mannesmann, SBC and British Telecommunications and the grouping of Bouygues and Italy's STET.

"We want a pricing structure that is not excessively advantageous to any of the sides," Bon said. "We want a pricing structure that will grow the market because when you are market leader you stand to gain most from the market growth."
